title: Mouse Without Borders Debug Output Active in Production Version
summary: Mouse Without Borders logging is reaching debugger-visible Trace output in release installs, and current logging code shows that routine MWB Log calls flow through ManagedCommon.Logger.LogInfo(), which unconditionally writes Trace lines.

judgment.rationale: The report is already concrete, and the current logging pipeline clearly routes ordinary Mouse Without Borders logging through an always-on Trace.WriteLine path in production builds.
evidence: The issue reports that a standard PowerToys install floods debugger output with Mouse Without Borders messages instead of keeping them confined to normal logs.
src/modules/MouseWithoutBorders/App/Core/Logger.cs routes routine MWB Logger.Log(...) calls to ManagedCommon.Logger.LogInfo(...).
src/common/ManagedCommon/Logger.cs implements LogInfo by calling a shared Log(...) method that unconditionally writes Trace.WriteLine output.

ManagedCommon.Logger.InitializeLogger(...) also adds a TextWriterTraceListener for the log file in all builds, so normal release logging is explicitly wired through the Trace pipeline rather than through a debugger-silent file-only path.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a focused logging-path fix that preserves supportable MWB file logs while stopping routine release logging from always appearing in debugger output.

fix_assessment.rationale: No public fix attempt is linked, and the current MWB-to-ManagedCommon logging path already exposes a concrete code-level cause.

issue_context.summary: Mouse Without Borders currently sends ordinary release logging through Trace, which is why developers see large amounts of MWB output even when they are not intentionally enabling a verbose diagnostic mode.
known_information: The report is on PowerToys 0.100.0 from the auto-updater and describes noisy output in a standard install.
A follow-up commenter confirmed the same pain point and suggested broader logging configurability.
The issue does not request removal of all logs; it asks for normal production behavior without always-on debug-style noise and mentions opt-in configurability as a welcome improvement.
No assignee or linked fix is present.
inferences: The immediate bug is narrower than a full ILogger migration: ordinary release logging is currently using a debugger-visible Trace path by default.
A complete logging redesign may be optional; the first-value fix is to separate supportable file logging from always-on debugger-output emission.
issue_context.analysis: This is ready for a focused design/start decision. The current source already explains the reported symptom and narrows the fix surface to the MWB/ManagedCommon logging path.
initial_investigation: src/modules/MouseWithoutBorders/App/Core/Logger.cs stamps and forwards routine log lines with ManagedCommon.Logger.LogInfo(...).
src/common/ManagedCommon/Logger.cs uses Trace.WriteLine for LogInfo, LogWarning, LogError, and LogTrace, while only LogDebug is conditional on DEBUG.
Because InitializeLogger adds a TextWriterTraceListener in all builds, the existing logger can preserve file logs even if debugger-facing trace emission is narrowed or made opt-in.

actions.label: Approve MWB logging-noise fix
actions.note: High-confidence logging issue: routine Mouse Without Borders release logs are flowing through an unconditional Trace pipeline.

proposed_fixes.title: Separate routine release logging from always-on debugger trace output
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Mouse Without Borders forwards ordinary release log lines to ManagedCommon.Logger.LogInfo(), and ManagedCommon.Logger implements that path with unconditional Trace.WriteLine calls, so routine production logging shows up in debugger output by default.
plan: Refactor the MWB/ManagedCommon logging path so normal release Info logging still reaches the support log file without always emitting debugger-visible Trace output.
If verbose debugger tracing is still needed, make it opt-in through a dedicated diagnostic mode or narrower trace path instead of the default release logging behavior.
Verify that existing support scenarios still capture the needed log file content after the debugger-noise reduction.
verification: Run a release or packaged build with Mouse Without Borders active and confirm routine operation no longer floods debugger output or DebugView by default.
Confirm the normal PowerToys/Mouse Without Borders log files still contain the expected support diagnostics for the same scenario.

confidence.rationale: The current code path maps directly to the reported symptom: ordinary MWB logging goes through a shared logger that unconditionally writes Trace output in production.
